correctness.rationale: For every r>=3, s>=1, q>rho(T) the exact clique/star diagonal resolvents are positive; the rank-one Schur complement at any fixed recipient vertex gives a unique coupling threshold. Strict within-block connector dominance, verified for both leaves and other clique vertices, leaves exactly two possible maxima. Comparing the two explicit resolvents gives a linear numerator in q and the candidate crossing qstar. Its position above rho(T) is equivalent to a positive quadratic C_r(s) and hence to integer r<=s<zeta_r. All boundary and equality cases are covered. The seven-vertex witness is exact; standalone rational checks test independent finite consequences without claiming exhaustive proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact all-integer clique/star leaf-count and all-admissible-recovery-ratio classification of which of two connector vertices minimizes one weighted SIS coupling threshold, not the classical spectral invasion criterion or resolvent Schur complement. The source comparison covers the 2026 local spectral threshold article; the stronger 2012–2013 general interconnection framework; and resolvent/eigenvector centrality literature. None of the inspected statements or sections supplies the sharp quadratic leaf-count frontier or the universal one-crossing family law. Priority remains limited to best-knowledge inspected material.
residual_risks: Classical Schur complements and spectral graph joining identities may appear in additional unindexed graph-theory papers; their existence alone does not settle the new sharp clique–star phase claim.

value.rationale: An internally coupled dense clique and star form a natural simplest network with competing spectral and high-degree candidate bridge endpoints. The derived exact sharp leaf-count boundary and recovery-ratio crossover characterize all infinitely many such communities and every subcritical receiving network. The switch gives a non-obvious consequence for contact placement: the same high-degree hub may or may not be the most threshold-threatening endpoint depending on recovery ratio. The exact algebraic classification is directly useful for interpreting local-versus-global spectral epidemic thresholds, not an arbitrary numerical parameter slice.
